nodes.title: Merkle Tree Certificates (draft-ietf-plants-merkle-tree-certs-07) + Chrome Quantum-resistant Root Store plan
nodes.summary: MTC is a PLANTS WG document, rev -07 dated 2026-10-07. IETF 126 (2026-07-20) minutes: 'should be ready to implement now'; OpenSSL (Bob Beck) and Cloudflare (Bas Westerbaan) committed to implement. Chrome (2026-02-27): no plan to add PQ X.509 to Chrome Root Store; Phase 1 Cloudflare feasibility study, Phase 2 Q1 2027 CT log operators bootstrap public MTCs, Phase 3 Q3 2027 Chrome Quantum-resistant Root Store (MTC-only), ACME-only, revocation limited to key compromise.
nodes.specifics: IETF125 experiment (Valenta, 2026-03-16): 1000 Cloudflare domains, 50% of Chrome Beta 146+, landmarks hourly, max inclusion proof 512 B (web scale 700-800 B), client landmark state ~10 KB, 7-day validity, P50 105 ms vs 116 ms (-9%), P90 348 vs 380 ms (-8%) vs classical ECDSA chains; 0.5-1.5% clients stale; middlebox interference non-factor.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Experiment backs every MTC with classical X.509 and uses classical sigs; PQ benefit is projected not measured. Dates are plans.
nodes.underclaim_risk: MTC is not vaporware: real traffic secured since early 2026, two browser vendors (Chrome, Apple per sibling rec60 node) aligned.
nodes.mandatory_for: Chrome CQRS public PQ auth from Q3 2027 (plan)

nodes.summary: AuthKEM (KEM-based server auth for TLS 1.3) is at -07 (2026-05-04), individual submission, not adopted by TLS WG. WebPKI PQ auth momentum is MTC (PLANTS) not KEMTLS.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Do not design around KEMTLS for public web.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Could matter for private mTLS where both ends are ours.

nodes.title: draft-ietf-tls-key-share-prediction-05 (DNS-hinted key shares) and its downgrade security considerations
nodes.summary: WG draft rev -05 (2026-10-15). Its security-considerations section is cited by rustls GHSA-w44r-93j7-qv28 as the reason a client's cached group prediction can be poisoned to classical-only if servers accept the offered share instead of HRR.

nodes.title: CNSA 2.0 timeline (NSA): web browsers/servers/cloud prefer by 2025, exclusive by 2033; signing exclusive by 2030
nodes.summary: NSA CNSA 2.0: software/firmware signing support+prefer by 2025, exclusive by 2030; web browsers/servers and cloud services support+prefer by 2025, exclusive by 2033; traditional networking equipment prefer 2026 exclusive 2030; OS prefer 2027 exclusive 2033; overall quantum-resistant NSS by 2035 (NSM-10). Algorithms: ML-KEM-1024, ML-DSA-87, LMS/XMSS (firmware), AES-256, SHA-384/512. Implication: X25519MLKEM768 does NOT satisfy CNSA 2.0; a gov mode needs SecP384r1MLKEM1024 or pure ML-KEM-1024 (rustls 0.23.37 added ML-KEM-1024).
nodes.overclaim_risk: Secondary sources; NSA PDF not fetched this round; 2031 vs 2033 discrepancy in one source.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Gov adoption requires this; ignoring it forecloses the enterprise/government axis.
nodes.mandatory_for: US NSS: web servers exclusive 2033; code signing exclusive 2030

nodes.summary: csrc.nist.gov page (fetched 2026-10-24) lists only the IPD; no 2pd or final. Draft: 112-bit RSA/ECC deprecated after 2030, all quantum-vulnerable public-key disallowed after 2035. Vendor reports of OMB memo alignment unverified.

nodes.summary: Cloudflare: <3% early 2024 -> ~35% Mar 2025 -> 52% (2025 Year in Review) -> >60% Feb 2026 -> >65% April 2026 (roadmap post; CF targets full PQ incl. authentication by 2029). nodes.title: rustls PQ posture: X25519MLKEM768 preferred by default since 0.23.27 (2025-05-05); ML-KEM-1024 0.23.37; ML-DSA certs default 0.23.44
nodes.summary: 0.23.22 (2025-01-30) X25519MLKEM768 supported at low priority; 0.23.27 adds prefer-post-quantum to default features; DEFAULT_KX_GROUPS (rel-0.23) = [X25519MLKEM768, X25519, SECP256R1, SECP384R1]; SECP256R1MLKEM768 opt-in (0.23.28); MLKEM768 and MLKEM1024 pure only in ALL_KX_GROUPS; 0.23.37 (2026-02-24) ML-KEM-1024; 0.23.44 (2026-09-07) ML-DSA cert verification on by default with aws-lc-rs (private PKI). Latest 0.23.46 (2026-10-14); main = 0.24.0-dev.2. Server group selection follows client's supported_groups order and sends HRR when no share -> rustls servers are not exploitable by the key-share-prediction downgrade.
nodes.specifics: L5: rustls = "=0.23.46" (>=0.23.46 required: GHSA-w44r, GHSA-2mjx, GHSA-c8m5, GHSA-h2v8). Config: default provider aws-lc-rs; gov profile kx_groups=[SECP384R1MLKEM1024?]/MLKEM1024 — NOTE rustls exposes MLKEM1024 pure but SecP384r1MLKEM1024 hybrid not seen in kx_group list (verify); disable brotli cert decompression unless needed; never Debug-format sessions. Perf: rustls absorbs most ML-KEM cost and still beats OpenSSL 3.3.2-X25519 except client resumption (Xeon E-2386G, CPU-only).
nodes.overclaim_risk: CPU-only perf; network bytes (~1.2 KB extra per direction) not in benchmark.
nodes.cve_count: GHSA 7 total (CVE-2024-32650 + 6 GHSA w/o CVE; 5 in 2026)
nodes.unsafe: 6 unsafe sites / 45.7 kLOC non-test (regex count, main 2026-10-23)
nodes.verified_parts: none in rustls itself; crypto via aws-lc-rs (partly verified) or libcrux/graviola providers

nodes.title: rustls 2026 advisories: epoch-boundary handshake acceptance, PQ key-share-prediction downgrade, Debug secret leak, brotli 1 GiB pre-auth
nodes.summary: GHSA-2mjx-qc3c-rqvc (2026-09-14, medium): 0.23.13..0.23.44 accepted plaintext handshake messages packed after ServerHello across encryption-level boundary (analog of Go CVE-2025-61730; reporter randombit). 2026-10-14 batch fixed in 0.23.46: GHSA-c8m5-c952-6cm4 (Session Debug exposes master secrets/PSKs, medium); GHSA-h2v8-394m-p7vv (brotli cert decompression up to 1 GiB before auth, low); GHSA-w44r-93j7-qv28 (unauthenticated ServerHello poisons per-name group cache -> later ClientHellos carry only X25519 => HNDL exposure if server accepts share, low); GHSA-vp88-798v-h67f (ECH rejection buffered data).
nodes.specifics: Invariant (L5): PQ-downgrade-resistance — for any client config with X25519MLKEM768 in supported_groups, no unauthenticated input may change the next ClientHello's key_share set; server invariant: if client lists a PQ hybrid group supported by server, server selects it (HRR if needed) — never a classical share. Test: replay harness that sends a classical-only ServerHello then asserts next ClientHello includes 0x11EC share.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Severity mostly low/medium; no auth bypass.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Memory-safe TLS still has protocol-state bugs at ~5/yr; a PQ posture can be silently downgraded by caching logic.

nodes.title: PQ size/MTU reality: hybrid KEM +~1.2 KB each way; ML-DSA chain +~14.7 KB; tldr.fail split-ClientHello breakage; QUIC 3x amplification forces extra RTT
nodes.summary: X25519MLKEM768 client share 1216 B (32+1184), server share 1120 B (32+1088) -> ClientHello exceeds one TCP segment/QUIC Initial. tldr.fail documented servers/middleboxes that did a single read() and reset: Vercel (fixed 2023-08-23), Zscaler (2023-09-28), Palo Alto (2025-03-27), Broadcom ProxySG 7.3.22.1, Apache Traffic Server (2025-06-25), Envoy (config), ingress-nginx passthrough, Cisco (unknown). Chrome measured ~4% handshake slowdown from hybrid KEM bytes. Cloudflare: ML-DSA-44 WebPKI handshake adds ~14.7 kB (2x1312 B pk + 5x2420 B sigs incl. 2 SCTs); SLH-DSA ~39 kB; CF 2021 experiment: >10 kB extra -> steep client/middlebox failure increase, <9 kB -> ~15% slower. QUIC: RFC 9000 3x anti-amplification; CoNEXT'22: 35% of classical cert chains already exceed it, 38% of handshakes need >1 RTT; an ML-DSA chain (~15-18 kB) cannot fit a ~3.6-7.5 kB budget -> guaranteed extra RTT(s) unless MTC (proof <=800 B) or cert compression.
nodes.specifics: L5 acceptance tests: (1) TLS listener must accept a ClientHello delivered 1 byte per read (fragmented-ClientHello fuzz case); (2) QUIC listener: measure handshake RTTs with 1200-B and 1350-B client Initials and a ML-DSA-65 private-PKI chain; budget <=2 RTT with RFC 8879 compression on; (3) PQ-auth path not offered on public listener until MTC.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Derived QUIC budget numbers (E) combine B-grade inputs.
nodes.underclaim_risk: KEM-only PQ is cheap (~4%); size problem is authentication, not key agreement.

nodes.title: Verified ML-KEM implementations in production: mlkem-native in AWS-LC (CBMC + HOL Light), libcrux in OpenSSH (hax/F*), Go/BoringSSL (non-verified but audited)
nodes.summary: mlkem-native (PQCA): C proven memory/type-safe with CBMC (191 ML-KEM proofs; 193 ML-DSA in mldsa-native), AArch64/x86_64 asm proven functionally correct + constant-time in HOL Light/s2n-bignum (36 ML-KEM, 27 ML-DSA proofs) per AWS HCSS 2026 deck; used by AWS-LC (FIPS cert #5298/#5314 include ML-KEM). OpenSSH: 10.0 made mlkem768x25519-sha256 default; openssh-portable vendors libcrux (Eurydice-extracted C from hax-verified Rust) via mlkem_mldsa.sh (OpenBSD rev 2026-06-14) incl. ML-DSA-44/65/87; OpenSSH 10.6 (2026-10-06) enables ssh-mldsa44-ed25519 and sshd WarnWeakCrypto by default. libcrux releases 2026-10-07; GHSA-435g-fcv3-8j26 (2026-02-12) bugs in libcrux-ecdh/ed25519/psq (not ML-KEM). Side channels: KyberSlash (2024) and Clangover CVE-2024-37880 (clang<=18 secret-dependent branch, ML-KEM-512 key recovery) — no new 2025-26 ML-KEM timing CVE found.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Proof scope: CBMC proves memory/type safety of C, not functional correctness; HOL Light covers asm kernels; spec bugs found in libcrux F* specs (sibling node fail-libcrux-spec-bugs-2026).
nodes.underclaim_risk: Verified PQ KEMs are in default code paths of AWS-LC and OpenSSH today — usable from Rust via aws-lc-rs or libcrux-ml-kem.

nodes.title: Release signing PQ options: LMS/XMSS (SP 800-208, stateful; CNSA firmware), SLH-DSA (stateless, 7.8-49.8 KB sigs), ML-DSA; Sigstore picked ML-DSA+SLH-DSA, excluded LMS
nodes.summary: SLH-DSA signature sizes: SHA2-128s 7,856 B, 128f 17,088 B, 192s 16,224 B, 256s 29,792 B, 256f 49,856 B; pk 32-64 B (IETF126 slides). SP 800-208 (Oct 2020) approves LMS/XMSS (stateful; state reuse = forgery). Sigstore (2025 post + POLICY.md): ML-DSA and SLH-DSA chosen for experiments, LMS excluded for state; Go LMS/ML-DSA implementations; no confirmed Rekor production ML-DSA by Oct 2026. CNSA 2.0 requires PQ code signing exclusively by 2030.
nodes.specifics: L5: dual-sign releases Ed25519 + SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s (stateless, 7.8 KB, hash-only assumption) now; optional ML-DSA-65; avoid LMS unless HSM-managed state; verifier in updater accepts if both verify (AND-composition).
nodes.underclaim_risk: SLH-DSA size is irrelevant for release artifacts (MBs).

nodes.title: hyper 1.12.0 / h2 0.4.20 (2026-10-06): DoS defaults and advisory record
nodes.summary: hyper v1.12.0 and h2 v0.4.20 released 2026-10-06. h2 advisories: CVE-2023-26964 (2023-04), GHSA-8r5v-vm4m-4g25 (2024-01 resource exhaustion), GHSA-q6cp-qfwq-4gcv (2024-04 CONTINUATION flood), GHSA-q83h-524g-xf6h (2026-08-17 unbounded empty DATA frames, fixed h2 0.4.16, low). MadeYouReset CVE-2025-8671: h2 'negligibly affected' — existing local-reset counter caught most variants, one missed WINDOW_UPDATE path fixed 2025-06-30 (h2 >=0.4.11 / 0.3.27), no advisory issued. hyper h1 smuggling history all 2017-2021 (CVE-2017-18587, CVE-2020-35863, CVE-2021-21299, CVE-2021-32714, CVE-2021-32715). Defaults (master): h2 DEFAULT_REMOTE_RESET_STREAM_MAX 20, DEFAULT_LOCAL_RESET_COUNT_MAX 1024, RESET_STREAM_MAX 50/1s, send buffer 400 KiB, empty-DATA cap, CONTINUATION count bounded by header-list/frame size; hyper server max_concurrent_streams 200, windows 1 MiB, max header list 16 KiB. hyper h1 chunk decoder requires CRLF (bare LF in extension -> error), CHUNKED_EXTENSIONS_LIMIT 16 KiB, checked size overflow.
nodes.specifics: L5 pins: hyper = "=1.12.0", h2 = ">=0.4.20". Config: http2 max_concurrent_streams 100-200, max_pending_accept_reset_streams Some(20), max_local_error_reset_streams Some(1024), max_header_list_size 16 KiB, keep_alive_interval set; must drain or cap bodies (GHSA-q83h precondition). Fuzz: reuse OSS-Fuzz hyperium targets (fuzz_client, fuzz_e2e, fuzz_hpack) + add h1 server target (hyper h1 not in OSS-Fuzz).
nodes.overclaim_risk: Low CVE count partly reflects small attacker attention vs nginx.
nodes.underclaim_risk: h2's reset accounting pre-empted MadeYouReset — an existence proof that budget-based design generalizes.

nodes.title: OSS-Fuzz coverage map for the network front (google/oss-fuzz projects tree, 1395 projects, 2026-10-24)
nodes.summary: Enrolled: rustls, hyperium (http+h2 targets), httparse, quiche-cloudflare, msquic, tokio, nom, quic-go, picotls, nghttp2, h2o, nginx, haproxy, envoy, boringssl, openssl. NOT enrolled: quinn, s2n-quic, hyper (h1/server), hyperium/h3, tquic, picoquic, lsquic, aws-lc, aws-lc-rs, pingora, libcrux.
nodes.specifics: L5 CI gate: every network-facing crate in our dep tree either has an OSS-Fuzz project or a ClusterFuzzLite job in our repo with >=N CPU-hours/week; list maintained in SUPPLY_CHAIN.md.

nodes.title: HTTP/1.1 desync is alive: 0.CL / Expect-based / chunk-terminator classes (2025) => use HTTP/2 (or h2c) upstream
nodes.summary: Kettle 'HTTP/1.1 must die' (2025-08-06, upd 2025-10-17): new 0.CL, double-desync, Expect-based desync; Akamai CVE-2025-32094 (74 bounties, $221k), Cloudflare internal H2 desync (~24M sites), total >$350k. Thesis: upstream HTTP/1.1 is inherently ambiguous; HTTP/2+ upstream removes the class; H2->H1 downgrade adds a 4th length interpretation. Chunk line-terminator family: Go CVE-2025-22871 (bare LF, fixed 1.23.8/1.24.2), Python h11 CVE-2025-43859 (CVSS 9.1). hyper rejects bare LF in chunk lines (code read 2026-10-13).
nodes.specifics: L5 invariant (parser canonicality): for every byte stream S accepted by our h1 parser, re-serializing parse(S) and re-parsing yields identical message boundaries; reject: CL+TE together, duplicate CL with differing values, TE other than exactly 'chunked', bare LF/CR anywhere in framing, obs-fold, Expect on bodyless methods, body on GET/HEAD/OPTIONS (configurable). Upstream: speak HTTP/2 (h2c or TLS) to backends by default; if HTTP/1.1 upstream, regenerate framing (never forward client CL/TE verbatim). Differential fuzz vs nginx/HAProxy/hyper with HTTP Request Smuggler v3 probes.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Bounty totals describe deployments, not parser libraries.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Strict Rust parser alone is not enough: desync is a two-parser property — the fix is architectural (normalize + H2 upstream).

nodes.title: EverParse/3D: verified binary-format parser generator in production (Hyper-V vSwitch), Rust backend; fit for our binary framings, not HTTP/1 text
nodes.summary: PLDI'22: >100 message formats across 4 protocols in Hyper-V network virtualization replaced handwritten parsers; IETF123 slides: every packet through Hyper-V vSwitch validated (Win10/11/Azure). CCS'25 EverCBOR/PulseParse: verified C+Rust CBOR/COSE (Distinguished Artifact). Fit: HTTP/2 frame headers, QUIC varints/frames, PROXY protocol v2, CBOR tokens; HTTP/1.1 is text/ambiguous — 3D is a poor fit, use a hand-written state machine with differential testing.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Rust extraction path less mature than C.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Zero-proof-effort verified parsers already ship at hyperscale.

nodes.title: io_uring CVE record vs epoll (NVD, 2026-10-24): 40 (2025) and 54 (2026 YTD) vs epoll 8 and 11; Google kCTF 60%
nodes.summary: NVD keyword 'io_uring': 2022:10, 2023:15, 2024:38, 2025:40, 2026 YTD:54 (161 total; 44 of 2025-26 scored >=7.0). Controls: epoll 7/8/11 (2024/25/26); kTLS 5/4/4; tls_sw 7/5/9; XDP 37/48/67; AF_XDP 3/7/16; netfilter 100/62/173. Examples: CVE-2026-80713 (ring created after exec escapes restrictions), CVE-2026-45995 (zcrx corruption), CVE-2026-43366 (kbuf race, type confusion), ZDI-25-915 futex UAF LPE. Google (2023): 60% of kCTF submissions exploited io_uring; disabled on ChromeOS and Google production servers, seccomp-blocked for Android apps; Docker default seccomp blocks io_uring syscalls.
nodes.specifics: L5: default runtime = epoll (tokio/mio); io_uring opt-in feature, front process only; every sandboxed handler/worker process gets seccomp deny for io_uring_setup/enter/register (syscalls 425-427) — CI test asserts EPERM. Kernel CVEs are a local-attacker risk: relevant when attacker code (Wasm escape, compromised handler) runs on box.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Kernel CNA mass-CVE assignment since 2024 inflates all counts; counts are not exploitability.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Ratio vs epoll (~5x) and Google's production ban are strong signals.

nodes.title: io_uring vs epoll for network servers: drop-in gains small (0-10%); large gains need zero-copy/batching/redesign
nodes.summary: arXiv 2512.04859 (DBMS, 2025): without zero-copy, epoll only marginally slower; zero-copy rx up to 2.5x. Java HTTP/2 load test: 26.7k vs 24.7k rps (~8%). uWebSockets #1603: epoll beat io_uring at 8-16 KB messages (memory/cache footprint). Axboe: swapping notifiers alone doesn't exploit io_uring.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Loopback microbenchmarks dominate the evidence.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Zero-copy rx (zcrx) is a genuine 2x+ for bulk transfer on modern kernels.

nodes.title: XDP pre-filter: ~24-26 Mpps/core drop vs ~0.2-0.4 Mpps iptables/nftables per core
nodes.summary: XDP paper (Høiland-Jørgensen et al., CoNEXT 2018): ~24 Mpps per core drop; Red Hat docs: 26M pps on a single core with xdp-filter. Requires CAP_BPF/CAP_NET_ADMIN; eBPF/XDP CVE counts rising (XDP 48 in 2025, 67 in 2026 YTD), but not reachable by unprivileged/sandboxed code if BPF syscall is seccomp-denied.
nodes.specifics: L5: optional xdp-filter module (aya crate) for bare-metal; off on $5 VPS (virtio often generic-mode XDP only).

nodes.title: QUIC throughput reality: Chrome QUIC 45.2% slower than HTTP/2 at 1 Gbps (receiver CPU, no UDP GRO)
nodes.summary: WWW'24 'QUIC is not Quick Enough over Fast Internet': QUIC falls behind above ~500 Mbps; at 1 Gbps 45.2% slower than HTTP/2; root cause receiver-side packet processing; recommends UDP GRO. Combined with quinn/h3 maturity and quinn's 2026 advisory wave, HTTP/3 is a latency/mobility feature, not a throughput or security win.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Browser client side; server-side GSO/GRO stacks (quinn-udp uses GSO/GRO) do better.

protocol_implications: Default TLS: rustls =0.23.46 + aws-lc-rs provider, X25519MLKEM768 preferred (default), HRR to PQ when client lists it; ML-DSA cert verification only for private PKI; public certs stay ECDSA until MTC (Chrome CQRS plan Q3 2027).
FIPS profile pins aws-lc-rs ~1.17.4 (fips) -> AWS-LC FIPS v3 (CMVP #5314/#5298, ML-KEM approved); CI blocks 1.18.x in FIPS profile until FIPS v4 is certified.
CNSA 2.0 profile must use ML-KEM-1024-based groups (not X25519MLKEM768) and ML-DSA-87/LMS for signing; flagged as open seed.

Network front defaults to HTTP/1.1+HTTP/2 over TCP (hyper 1.12 / h2 0.4.20) with explicit DoS budgets; HTTP/3 (quinn/h3) is an opt-in feature because quinn had 11 DoS advisories in 2026, h3 is pre-1.0 and stale, and QUIC is slower at >500 Mbps.
Upstream to backends speaks HTTP/2 by default; HTTP/1.1 upstream regenerates framing; h1 parser canonicality invariant + differential fuzzing is a CI gate.
epoll (tokio/mio) default; io_uring opt-in for the front only; all sandboxed workers seccomp-deny io_uring_* syscalls (CI asserts EPERM).
Every network-facing dependency needs OSS-Fuzz or an in-repo ClusterFuzzLite job; advisory monitoring must poll repo-level GHSA (global DB lagged for quinn).
PQ downgrade-resistance invariant and fragmented-ClientHello acceptance test become part of SPEC_INVARIANTS/BENCH_PLAN.
Release signing: dual Ed25519 + SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s now (stateless), revisit ML-DSA when Sigstore ships it.
self_improvement: gh api repo-level security-advisories is a far better needle than web search for crate CVE lists (global GHSA DB lagged 7 of 11 quinn 2026 advisories). Add to META needle tactics.
datatracker HTTP redirect from draft name to /doc/rfcNNNN/ + rfc-editor JSON is a 1-call way to confirm a draft became an RFC; web search returned stale draft status.
CMVP certificate pages are scrapeable; algorithm lists answer 'does module X include ML-KEM' definitively — use instead of vendor blogs.
Shallow-clone + regex unsafe counting is cheap; but large repos (s2n-quic) need --filter=blob:limit and a timeout to avoid stalling.
